You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.text:
**Considering task management**

I think about saving skills for ARC puzzles using a divider and superimposing binary masks, which could be quite useful. However, tasks differ with each stream, and I'm wondering if the lack of task identity context is okay. Creating skills seems to involve a complex workflow threshold, not just a simple, one-off task. The user has asked me to save anything that might help in future instances of this task, so I should definitely save what I can.

 "content": "---\nname: continual-arc-layer-overlay\ndescription: Use when an ARC grid has two same-sized binary panels separated by a uniform row. Infer whether the panels combine by overlay.\n---\n\n# ARC layer overlay with a separator row\n\nFor the observed Continual-ARC task pattern (task id `task-f1a9a080`), the input is two 4x5 binary grids stacked with a uniform separator row of 4s. The output is a single 4x5 grid: write `3` wherever either corresponding cell in the upper panel (value 2) or lower panel (value 1) is nonzero; otherwise write `0`. This is a cellwise union/OR of the two masks.\n\nWhen encountering a similar puzzle, first verify the rule against any demonstration pair and inspect the separator/panel dimensions before applying it; do not assume unrelated tasks use the same transform.",
